# annals

Annals for AI agents. An agent publishes a document (markdown, html, an image, a video, a PDF, or a whole folder of renders) with one command and gets back a link; the owner opens their annals on a phone and finds everything their agents left for them, newest first, searchable, with a recycle bin.

```bash
pip install annals
annals publish report.md --session my-agent
# https://apps.example.com/annals/d/20261003-203301-quarterly-report-3f9a
```

Beside what agents publish, the page can list other folders read in place, such as the sessions’ ledgers (`~/.local/share/crowsnest/ledger`): one search over every word of every item, filters by source, kind, session, date and tag, and tags you add from the page, kept apart from the files.

Documents are plain files in a directory. The directory can be on this machine or on another one over ssh, and the page that serves it reads it directly, so publishing never redeploys anything. No database, no build step, no API token.

## For agents

Load the shipped skill, `annals-publish`, and you have the whole protocol: one command, one link, put the link in your reply.

```bash
annals publish report.md                          # one document, prints its link
annals publish a.md b.md c.html --group "Review"  # one link for a set (the group link prints first)
annals publish d.md --add-to <group-id>           # add to that set later (same link)
annals publish ./renders                          # a folder: a gallery with inline images, video, audio
annals publish ./site_dir                         # an html page with its assets, as one document
annals publish clip.mp4                           # media plays inline (streamed, seekable)
some-command | annals publish - --title "Log"     # from stdin
annals publish guide.html --replace <link-or-id>  # a new version of a document: same link
annals publish page.html --artifact <claude.ai artifact link>  # plus a button to its interactive version
annals ls "search words"                          # what is there, newest first
annals trash <id>  /  annals restore <id>         # the recycle bin
```

What each kind looks like on the page:

| Published                                      | Shown as                                                                                                                 |
|------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| a `.md` file                                   | rendered markdown, with a toggle to the source and a copy button; its relative images and links resolve to its own files |
| an `.html` file, or a folder with `index.html` | the page itself, in a sandboxed frame                                                                                    |
| an image, video, audio file or PDF             | inline: image, player (byte-range streaming, so video seeks), PDF viewer                                                 |
| a folder with one page in it                   | that page, with the other files below it                                                                                 |
| any other folder                               | a gallery: image thumbnails (a page at a time), players, a file list; every file opens on its own with prev/next         |
| anything else                                  | a download                                                                                                               |

A folder skips hidden files and caches (`.*`, `__pycache__`, `*.pyc`); `--all-files` keeps them.

### Interactive version (`--artifact`)

`annals publish page.html --artifact https://claude.ai/...` stores the link of a Claude Artifact holding the same page in the document’s meta (`artifact`), and the document’s page shows an “Open the interactive version” button next to the frame. Comments, per-viewer and shared state and sharing then live on the artifact while annals stays the single in-tray. Only plain `https` links to `claude.ai` are accepted (`annals.store.ARTIFACT_HOSTS`; no port, credentials or odd characters), `--artifact` takes one path, and a `--replace` without `--artifact` keeps the current link.

### Living pages (`--replace`)

`annals publish <path> --replace <link-or-id>` publishes a new version of an existing document: the id and the link stay, the page shows the new version marked “updated” and lists the earlier ones, each readable at `/d/<id>@<n>`. The previous files are kept under the document’s `.versions/<n>/`; nothing is deleted. It takes one path (a file, a folder, stdin), and a replaced group member stays in its group.

A replacement is written next to the document as a pending directory (`docs/<id>.r<stamp>-<hex>/`), never over it, and applied by whoever reads the store (the server, or the next publish): a few renames, the first of which claims the document, so concurrent readers never apply one twice or out of order. That is what lets a replace travel through an **outbox**, a directory another machine pulls and empties: mark it with `annals configure --outbox` (or `ANNALS_OUTBOX=1`), and replacements published there are left for the server to apply when they land. HTML pages without a doctype are served with `<!doctype html>` (plus a charset and viewport when missing), so they render in standards mode.

With `pip install 'annals[mcp]'`, the same operations are an MCP server: `python -m annals.mcp`.

## Where documents go

```bash
annals configure --target tw:/root/.local/share/annals --base-url https://apps.example.com/annals
```

That writes `~/.config/annals/config.toml`. `target` is a directory, or `host:/path` for a directory on another machine reached by `ssh host` (keys, no prompt; `host` can be an alias from `~/.ssh/config`). `ANNALS_TARGET` and `ANNALS_BASE_URL` override it per shell. With no configuration, documents go to `~/.local/share/annals` and the link points at a local `annals serve`.

### A second place (`--to`)

A config file can name more places: `annals configure --to team --target host:/path --base-url https://team.example.com/annals` saves a `[targets.team]` table and leaves the default alone. Then `annals publish r.md --to team` (also `ls`, `show`, `trash`, `restore`, `group`, `groups`) works on that place only, and `annals copy <link-or-id> --to team [--source other]` copies documents or whole groups there, keeping their ids. Nothing about the place is in the code: a name, a target and a base url.

## Hosting the page

**Inside an app platform** (the usual case). Mount the API under the platform’s prefix and let the platform’s login gate it:

```python
# server.py of the host app; the platform serves frontend/ at /annals/ and this at /api/annals
from annals.api import mk_api
app = mk_api(data_dir="/root/.local/share/annals")
```

and write the page shell once as the app’s frontend:

```bash
annals page-shell --api /api/annals --base /annals > frontend/index.html
```

The shell only names those two paths; the page’s script and style load from the API, so upgrading the package upgrades the page. Gallery thumbnails are made with Pillow when it is installed (cached under the data root’s `cache/`), and fall back to the original image when it is not.

**Standalone**, for a machine with no platform:

```bash
pip install 'annals[server]'
ANNALS_DATA_DIR=~/.local/share/annals annals serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765
```

The page is at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/annals/`, its API under `/annals/api/`. Auth is chosen by environment variables:

| Situation                                                 | Set                                                                                                   | Effect                                                                                                                        |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Behind an existing login that exposes a who-am-I endpoint | `ANNALS_WHOAMI_URL`, `ANNALS_ALLOWED_USERS=me@example.com`, optionally `ANNALS_LOGIN_URL=/auth/login` | the browser’s cookies are forwarded to that endpoint and the listed emails are allowed; anyone else is sent to the login page |
| No platform login                                         | `ANNALS_BASIC_USER`, `ANNALS_BASIC_PASSWORD`                                                          | HTTP Basic                                                                                                                    |
| Localhost only                                            | nothing                                                                                               | open                                                                                                                          |

## Sharing one page

The annals is private; a **share link** lets someone without an account read ONE document (or one group) and nothing else. From the page, the Share button on a document lists its files and the annals pages it links to, so you choose what goes; from a shell:

```bash
annals share <id-or-link> --password -                       # 7 days by default; password from stdin
annals share <id> --expires 2026-11-30                       # or 12h, 30d, an ISO time, `never`
annals share <id> --include img/chart.png,img/map.png        # only these files (the page always goes)
annals shares                                                # live links (--all: revoked and expired too)
annals unshare <link-or-token>                               # off at once
```

The link is `<share_base_url>/<token>/`: 128 random bits, `noindex`, `no-referrer`. Every request is checked against the share’s record (`shares/<token>.json` under the data root), so a file you did not choose is a 404 even beside the shared page, a revoke or an expiry takes effect on the next request, and references to anything outside the share (an image you left out, a link to another annals page or to anything else on your annals’ host, an annals id in the text) are removed from every text file before it is sent (markdown, html, plain text, svg). A linked page you tick goes with the files it shows, not every file beside it. The password is a gate on the link, not an account: at least 8 characters, stored hashed (stdlib scrypt), with attempts limited per client and per link, and a correct one earns a cookie scoped to that link. Links are read-only and last 7 days unless you say otherwise.

Where the links are served:

- **Standalone** (`annals serve`): at `/annals/shared/<token>/`, outside the login, with nothing to configure.
- **Inside an app platform**: the share server must be reachable without the platform’s login, so run it as its own public app and tell annals where it is:

```python
# server.py of a second, PUBLIC app (the owner's app keeps its login)
from annals.share_api import mk_share_api
app = mk_share_api(data_dir="/root/.local/share/annals")
```

then set `ANNALS_SHARE_BASE_URL` (or `annals configure --share-base-url ...`, or `mk_api(share_base_url=...)` for the owner’s page) to that app’s public URL. Until it is set, shares are made but carry no link. `mk_share_api` takes `rate_limiter=` and `link_failure_limiter=` (anything with `allow(key) -> bool`, such as heed’s Redis limiter; the defaults count per process), `trusted_proxies=` (whose `X-Forwarded-For` names the client; loopback by default) and `private_hosts=`; the password `hasher` is a keyword of `annals.share.Shares` (argon2, or anything with `hash`/`verify`).

## Downloads

Every markdown page has an **Actions** menu (Share, Copy, Download, View) with two downloads made by the server: **Markdown (.md)** and a titled **PDF** with the images inside (audio, video and other files appear as a link to the resource). Both are named after the title (`quarterly-report-q3.pdf`) and are served under the same rules as the page: the owner’s login, or a share link’s scope (a recipient gets the filtered text and only the files the link includes). The PDF needs `pip install "annals[pdf]"` (WeasyPrint, which uses Pango; `annals[server]` includes it); without it the PDF action answers with that hint. Pages (`/d/<id>`) are drawn in the browser by `app.js`, so a page that gains an action gains it for every existing document.

## Other folders, search, filters and tags

Name extra folders when you mount the API, and they appear beside the published documents, each in its own section (`/annals/s/<name>`) and in `/annals/all`:

```python
app = mk_api(data_dir="~/.local/share/annals", sources={"ledgers": "~/.local/share/crowsnest/ledger"})
```

or, with no code, `ANNALS_SOURCES="ledgers=~/.local/share/crowsnest/ledger"` (several: comma-separated). A folder is read in place and never written: its files are listed newest first with their age, markdown renders, html is framed, the rest shows by its kind, and a sub-folder’s files count as written by the sub-folder’s name. Hidden files and caches are skipped.

On every list:

- **Search** matches every word, case-insensitively, against titles, tags, sessions, excerpts and the full text of markdown and text files (on the server; the matching passage shows under the title).
- **Filters** are one button per family (source, kind, session, date, tag). Checked values within a family are alternatives (“any of”), families combine (“and”), the counts are what each choice would give now, and the active filters show as removable chips. The filters and the search are in the URL, so Back undoes a filter and a link reproduces the view.
- **Tags**: add or remove them on any item’s page; they save as you go. They are stored apart from the items, in one file under the data root (`tags/tags.json`), so a ledger is never touched; on a published document they replace the tags the publisher gave.

The API behind it: `GET /items?q=&source=&trash=` → `{data, total}`, `GET /items/<source>:<id>`, `PATCH /items/<source>:<id>` with `{"tags": [...]}`, `GET /tags`, `GET /sources`, and `GET /files/<source>/<path>` for a folder’s raw files. The page reaches items through [`@zodal/store-http`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zodal/store-http)’s provider (vendored; rebuild with `misc/vendor/build.sh`).

## Python API

```python
from annals import DocStore, publish
meta = DocStore("~/.local/share/annals").publish("report.md", tags=["q3"])
publish(["report.md"], tags="q3")["url"]          # same, through the configured target
```

`annals.api.mk_api(...)` is the mountable API; `annals.api.mk_app(data_dir=..., authorizer=...)` the standalone app. Both take `sources=` (name → folder path, or any `annals.sources.Source`) and `tags=` (any `MutableMapping` from item key to tag list; default `JsonTagStore`). `annals.catalog.Catalog` is the facade they stand on: every source’s rows as one list, searched, with the owner’s tags.

## Design notes

Flat store with tags and groups, not a hierarchy: agents from many projects do not share one, and every placement decision costs tokens. A document is `docs/<id>/meta.json` plus its files; the bin is `trash/<id>/`; a group is `groups/<gid>.json`. Ids are `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<slug>-<4 hex>`, so a listing is already in time order and a URL says what it points to. The transport is a seam (`annals.target`): local directory, ssh, and later an http ingest endpoint. More in `misc/docs/design.md`.

## Skills

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/annals annals-publish
```

The skill also ships inside the package at `annals/data/skills/annals-publish/`.

# _autosummary/annals.auth.html.md

# annals.auth

The auth seam: who may read the annals.

A annals is private by construction, so the server asks every request who is calling. The
answer comes from one of three `Authorizer` callables, chosen by [`authorizer_from_env()`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.authorizer_from_env)
(or passed to `annals.api.mk_app()`):

* [`no_auth()`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.no_auth): everyone is the owner. Right for `annals serve` bound to `127.0.0.1`,
  wrong anywhere else.
* [`CookieWhoami`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.CookieWhoami): forward the request’s cookies to an identity endpoint that answers
  `{"email": ...}` (enlace_auth’s `/auth/whoami`), and allow the listed emails. This is
  how a annals sits behind an existing login without owning passwords: the login page, the
  session cookie and the logout belong to the platform; the annals only checks the allowlist.
  Env: `ANNALS_WHOAMI_URL`, `ANNALS_ALLOWED_USERS` (comma separated), `ANNALS_LOGIN_URL`.
* [`BasicAuth`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.BasicAuth): one username and password (HTTP Basic). For a annals with no platform
  login in front of it. Env: `ANNALS_BASIC_USER`, `ANNALS_BASIC_PASSWORD`.

An authorizer returns the caller’s identity (a string) or `None`. The API turns `None`
into a 303 to the login page for a browser GET, and a 401 for anything else, mirroring
what enlace_auth does so the two are indistinguishable from the phone.

|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`no_auth`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.no_auth)(request)             | Everyone is `owner`.                                                       |

# _autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md

# annals.catalog

The catalog: every source’s items as one list, with search and the owner’s tags.

[`Catalog`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog) is the facade the HTTP API stands on. It combines named sources (see
[`annals.sources`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#module-annals.sources)) and a tag store (see [`annals.tags`](_autosummary/annals.tags.html.md#module-annals.tags)):

* [`Catalog.rows()`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog.rows) lists items newest first, across sources or within one, filtered by
  a full-text query (every word must appear in the title, tags, session, excerpt or full
  text; case-insensitive), each row with the owner’s tags overlaid and, when there is a
  query, a `snippet` of the text around the first match.
* [`Catalog.item()`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog.item) is one item, [`Catalog.set_tags()`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog.set_tags) replaces its tags (in the tag
  store, never in the item), [`Catalog.tag_counts()`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog.tag_counts) lists every tag in use.

Facets (kind, session, date, tag) are not computed here: the page counts them over the rows
it received, so every toggle is instant and the counts are always the ones the current
query would give.

| [`mk_catalog`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.mk_catalog)(store, \*[, sources, tags])   | The published documents first, then the extra sources; the owner's tags beside them.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

The published documents first, then the extra sources; the owner’s tags beside them.

`sources` maps a name to a folder path (read in place) or a `Source`; by
default the folders named in `ANNALS_SOURCES`. `tags` defaults to one JSON file
under the data root (`tags/tags.json`), or a dict when the data root is remote.
The API, and any CLI or agent tool that tags items, build their catalog here.

* **Return type:**

# _autosummary/annals.config.html.md

# annals.config

Settings: where documents are published and what link to print.

Two values matter to a publisher:

* `target`: where the documents go. A directory (`~/.local/share/annals`) or an ssh
  destination (`tw:/root/.local/share/annals`). This is the data root the annals server
  reads, locally or on another machine.
* `base_url`: the public root of the annals app, so a publish can print the link the owner
  opens (`https://apps.example.com/annals`).
* `share_base_url`: where the public share server answers, so `annals share` prints the
  link a recipient opens (`<share_base_url>/<token>/`). It defaults to
  `<base_url>/shared`, which is where `annals serve` mounts it; a platform that runs the
  share server as its own public app sets it (`ANNALS_SHARE_BASE_URL` or the config file).

Resolution order, highest first: explicit keyword arguments, environment variables
(`ANNALS_TARGET`, `ANNALS_BASE_URL`), the config file (`$ANNALS_CONFIG` or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/annals/config.toml`, default `~/.config/annals/config.toml`), then the
local defaults (publish into the local data dir, link to a local `annals serve`).

Named targets (`--to NAME`): a second place to publish, opted into per command. The config
file holds them as `[targets.NAME]` tables with the same two keys; `annals configure --to
NAME --target ... --base-url ...` writes one. `to` picks it over the environment and the
file’s default, and explicit `target`/`base_url` arguments still win over `to`.

A third, `outbox`, is true for a target another machine pulls and empties (the server
fetches documents from it rather than being written to): a replacement published there
travels as it is and is applied where it lands (see [`annals.store`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#module-annals.store)). `ANNALS_OUTBOX`
overrides it.

The server side has two knobs of its own. `ANNALS_DATA_DIR` is the directory the API
reads. It defaults to `~/.local/share/annals`, which is also the default publish target,
so with no configuration at all `annals publish` and `annals serve` meet in the same
place. `ANNALS_SOURCES` names extra folders the page lists beside the published documents,
read in place (`ledgers=~/.local/share/crowsnest/ledger`; several, comma-separated).

### Module Attributes

| [`ENV_SHARE_BASE_URL`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.ENV_SHARE_BASE_URL)   | where the public share server answers (a share link is `<this>/<token>/`)   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ENV_SOURCES`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.ENV_SOURCES)          | "name=path, name2=path2"                                                    |

### Functions

| [`default_config_path`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.default_config_path)()                          | `$ANNALS_CONFIG`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/annals/config.toml`.                      |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`default_data_dir`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.default_data_dir)()                             | The local data root: `$ANNALS_DATA_DIR` or `~/.local/share/annals`.                |
| [`load_settings`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.load_settings)(\*[, target, base_url, to, ...]) | Resolve settings: arguments, then `to`, env, the config file, then local defaults. |
| [`named_targets`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.named_targets)(\*[, config_path])               | The `[targets.NAME]` tables of the config file: name -> {target, base_url}.        |
| [`write_config`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.write_config)(settings, \*[, to, config_path])  | Write the config file (string keys only; no TOML writer dependency needed).        |

# _autosummary/annals.html.md

# annals

annals: an in-tray for AI agents. Publish documents and media to a private page; get a link.

Agents call [`annals.tools.publish()`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.publish) (or `annals publish file.md` from a shell) and hand
the printed URL to their human, who opens it on a phone. The documents are plain files in a
directory, local or on another machine over ssh; `annals.api.mk_app()` serves that
directory as a private page with search, sort, groups and a recycle bin.

### Functions

| [`configure`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.configure)(\*[, target, base_url, to, outbox, ...])   | Write the publisher config (where to publish, what link to print) and show it.                                                                                    |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`group`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.group)(title, doc_ids, \*[, target, base_url, to])    | Make a group (one URL for a set of documents) from existing document ids.                                                                                         |
| [`groups`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.groups)(\*[, target, base_url, to])                   | List groups, newest first.                                                                                                                                        |
| [`load_settings`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.load_settings)(\*[, target, base_url, to, ...])       | Resolve settings: arguments, then `to`, env, the config file, then local defaults.                                                                                |
| [`ls`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.ls)([q, trash, limit, target, base_url, to])          | List documents (newest first), optionally filtered by words or showing the bin.                                                                                   |
| [`parse_target`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.parse_target)(spec)                                   | `host:/path` becomes an [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.SshTarget); anything else a [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.LocalTarget). |
| [`publish`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.publish)(paths, \*[, title, tags, group, ...])        | Publish one document and print its link; several paths become several documents.                                                                                  |
| [`restore`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.restore)(doc_ids, \*[, target, to])                   | Bring documents back from the recycle bin.                                                                                                                        |
| [`show`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.show)(doc_id, \*[, target, base_url, to])             | A document's metadata and link (`to`: on a named target).                                                                                                         |
| [`trash`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.trash)(doc_ids, \*[, target, to])                     | Move documents to the recycle bin (restorable).                                                                                                                   |

#### meta(doc_id, , settle=True)

One document’s meta; `in_trash` says which side of the bin it is on.

`<id>@<n>` is version `n`: its own meta, with `version_of` naming the document.
A pending replacement, read by its own id, says `pending`. `settle=False`
skips applying pending replacements (for a hot path such as a raw file).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

Pending replacements (directory names), oldest first; of one document if given.

`names`: the listing of `docs/` when the caller already has it.

* **Return type:**

#### publish(\*sources, title=None, tags=(), source=None, text=None, filename='document.md', exclude=('.\*', '_\_pycache_\_', '\*.pyc', '\*.pyo'), replace=None, artifact=None)

Publish files (or a directory, or `text`) as ONE document; return its meta.

One markdown or html file is the common case. A directory is published whole, with
`index.html` (or the first renderable file) as the page shown. `text` publishes a
string as `filename` instead of reading sources. `exclude` lists glob patterns
skipped inside a directory (hidden files and caches by default; `()` keeps all).

`replace` (a document id) publishes a new version of that document instead of a
new document: same id, same link, the current files kept as a version. It is
written as a pending replacement and applied at once when this store settles
(otherwise where the store is read). The returned meta says `pending` until then.

`artifact` (a claude.ai artifact link, see `check_artifact_url()`) is the
interactive version of the page: the document’s page links out to it. A
replacement that names none keeps the document’s current one.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

* **Return type:**

A replacement whose document is not here yet (it is still on its way, or the

* **Return type:**

### annals.configure(, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, outbox=False, share_base_url=None)

Write the publisher config (where to publish, what link to print) and show it.

### Example

`annals configure --target tw:/root/.local/share/annals --base-url https://apps.example.com/annals`.
`--to NAME` saves the target and base url as a named target (`annals publish --to NAME`)
and leaves the default alone. `--outbox` marks the target as an outbox: a directory
the server pulls and empties (it cannot be written to from here), so replacements are
left for the server to apply; it is kept by later changes (`ANNALS_OUTBOX=0` or an
edit of the file turns it off). `--share-base-url` is where share links point when
the share server is not at `<base-url>/shared` (a platform running it as its own
public app). With no arguments, shows the resolved settings without writing.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.publish(paths, , title=None, tags='', group=None, add_to=None, session=None, all_files=False, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, replace=None, artifact=None)

Publish one document and print its link; several paths become several documents.

`paths`: files of any kind (markdown, html, images, video, audio, pdf, text), a
directory (one document: an `index.html` or single page with its assets, else a
gallery of everything in it), or `-` for stdin (markdown). `tags` is comma separated. `group`
names a group to create from the published documents; the reply then carries
`group_url` too. `add_to` appends them to an existing group instead (its id, as
printed in a group link), so a second batch lands under the link the owner already has. `session` records who published (the source shown on the page). A directory skips
hidden files and caches (`.*`, `__pycache__`, `*.pyc`) unless `all_files`.
`to` publishes to a named target of the config file (`[targets.NAME]`, see
`annals configure --to`) instead of the default one. `replace` (a document’s link or
id) publishes ONE path as a new version of that document: the link stays the same, the
page shows the new version and offers the earlier ones. That is how a living page (a
guide, a status page) keeps one link. `artifact` (a claude.ai artifact link) is the
interactive version of the page: the document’s page shows an “Open the interactive
version” button. Publish the Artifact first, then the same page here with its link.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.restore(doc_ids, , target=None, to=None)

Bring documents back from the recycle bin.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# _autosummary/annals.share.html.md

# annals.share

Share links: one document (or a group) behind a public, unguessable, revocable link.

A share is a record under the data root, `shares/<token>.json`, written through the
same [`annals.target.Target`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.Target) as the documents, so `annals share` works over ssh
exactly like `annals publish`. The record is the whole contract; the owner’s API, the
page’s Share button, the CLI and the public share server (`annals.share_api`) are
surfaces over it:

```default
{
 "token": "<22 url-safe chars, 128 random bits>",
 "title": "...", "created": "<iso>",
 "root": {"kind": "doc" | "group", "id": "<id>"},
 "docs": {"<doc id>": ["<file>", ...], ...},   # what the link may reach, and only that
 "expires": "<iso>" | null,
 "password": "scrypt$..." | null,               # a hash; the password is never stored
 "revoked": "<iso>" | null                       # a tombstone: a revoked link is a 404
}
```

`docs` is the scope. Every request of the public server is checked against it, never
against what the link was made from: a file not listed is a 404 even when it sits beside
the shared page, and a page or a link of the shared text that points outside the scope is
removed before the text leaves the server ([`filter_refs()`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.filter_refs)), so the recipient sees
neither private ids nor private paths.

The link itself (the token, the password gate, expiry, revocation) is a
`caplinks.CapabilityLinks` over these records; what is annals’ own is the scope
and the filtering. The password is a gate on the link, not an account: anyone who knows
both may read. It is hashed (stdlib `scrypt` by default, the `hasher` seam takes
argon2), and a correct one earns an HMAC cookie keyed by that hash, so changing the
password or revoking the link ends every open session.

### Module Attributes

| [`ANNALS_ID`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.ANNALS_ID)   | an annals id (doc or group) as [`annals.store.mk_id()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.mk_id) makes them   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`dir_of`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.dir_of)(rel)                                       | The directory part of a relative path, with its trailing slash (`""` at the top).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`filter_refs`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.filter_refs)(text, kind, \*, files, shared[, ...]) | `text` with every reference outside the share removed (or rewritten).               |
| [`references`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.references)(text, kind, \*[, from_dir])            | What a page points at: files of its document, and annals pages (by id).             |
| [`resolve_rel`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.resolve_rel)(url[, from_dir])                      | A relative url as a file path inside the document, or `None` if it is not one.      |
| [`share_url`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.share_url)(base, token)                            | The link a recipient opens, or `None` when no share server is configured.           |

### Classes

| [`Shares`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.Shares)(store, \*[, hasher, clock])   | Create, read, list and revoke shares of a `DocStore`'s documents.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|

### annals.share.ANNALS_ID *= '\\\\d{8}-\\\\d{6}-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)\*'*

an annals id (doc or group) as [`annals.store.mk_id()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.mk_id) makes them

### *class* annals.share.Shares(store, \*, hasher=None, clock=<function now_utc>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Create, read, list and revoke shares of a `DocStore`’s documents.

What a share reaches (its scope) is decided here; the link itself is `links`, a
`caplinks.CapabilityLinks` over the records under `shares/`. `hasher`
hashes link passwords (stdlib scrypt by default); `clock` returns the current UTC
`datetime` (tests pin it).

#### check_password(record, password)

Whether `password` opens `record`.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### create(ref, , include=None, exclude=(), password=None, expires='7d', title=None)

Share a document or a group (`ref` is its id); return the record (no hash).

A document is shared with all its files unless `include` names some (the page
itself always goes); `include` may also name annals pages the document links
to, which then open inside the share. A group is shared with all its documents
unless `include` names some. `exclude` removes files (or a group’s documents).
A linked page goes with the files it shows. `expires` is anything
`parse_expires()` reads, 7 days by default (`"never"` for none); `password`
gates the link (at least `caplinks.MIN_PASSWORD_LEN` characters).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### list(, all=False)

Every share, newest first, without hashes; `all` adds revoked and expired.

* **Return type:**

The stored record (hash included), revoked or not; `None` if there is none.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### resources(doc_id)

What the Share dialog offers for a document: its files, and the pages it links.

`{"main", "files": [{"rel", "kind", "size", "referenced"}], "pages": [{"id",
"title", "kind"}]}`. `referenced` marks the files the page itself shows or
links; `pages` are the other annals documents its text links to.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

End a link now (idempotent). The record stays, as a tombstone, for the list.

`("ok" | "expired" | "missing", record)`; a revoked link is `missing`.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

#### unlock_value(record)

The cookie value a correct password earns.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### unlocked(record, value, , max_age_s)

Whether a cookie value is a live unlock of this record (no password: always).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### annals.share.dir_of(rel)

The directory part of a relative path, with its trailing slash (`""` at the top).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.share.filter_refs(text, kind, , files, shared, from_dir='', private_hosts=())

`text` with every reference outside the share removed (or rewritten).

`files` are the document’s files the share includes; `shared(id)` maps an annals
id to where the recipient opens it (in scope) or `None` (not shared). A markdown
image out of scope disappears, a link keeps its words; an html attribute goes; a bare
annals url becomes “(link not shared)” and a bare annals id “(not shared)”. The text
of the page itself is the owner’s: only references are touched. An absolute url on
one of `private_hosts` (the owner’s own) goes too, whatever its path. Every kind of
text is filtered (markdown, html, plain text, svg): only markdown syntax is markdown’s.
Best effort by design, and the second line of defence: the share server answers 404
for anything outside the share however the text names it.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.share.references(text, kind, , from_dir='')

What a page points at: files of its document, and annals pages (by id).

`{"files": [rel, ...], "ids": [annals id, ...]}`, each in first-seen order; it
feeds the Share dialog, which offers them to the owner.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.share.resolve_rel(url, from_dir='')

A relative url as a file path inside the document, or `None` if it is not one.

```pycon
>>> resolve_rel("img/a.png?x=1#y", "notes/")
'notes/img/a.png'
>>> resolve_rel("../../etc/passwd") is None, resolve_rel("https://x.org/a") is None
(True, True)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

The link a recipient opens, or `None` when no share server is configured.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/annals.sources.html.md

# annals.sources

Item sources: everything the page lists, wherever it lives, as rows of one shape.

A *source* is a named, read-mostly collection of items. Two kinds exist:

* [`PublishedSource`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#annals.sources.PublishedSource): the documents agents published (a [`annals.store.DocStore`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore)).
* [`FolderSource`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#annals.sources.FolderSource): a folder of files owned by someone else, read in place and never
  written (the crowsnest ledgers, and any other personal folder later). Its items are the
  folder’s files, keyed by their path relative to the folder.

Every source yields the same row shape, which the page lists, searches and filters:

`key`      `<source>:<id>`, unique across sources (the API’s item id)
`source`   the source’s name; `id` the item’s id within it
`title`, `kind` (see [`annals.store.kind_of()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.kind_of)), `session` (who wrote it)
`time`     ISO 8601, UTC: publication time, or a file’s last modification
`size`, `tags` (the item’s own; the catalog overlays the owner’s), `excerpt`

Sources are plain objects with a few methods (the [`Source`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#annals.sources.Source) protocol), so a new kind
of folder is a new class or a new keyword argument, never a change to the API.

### Module Attributes

### *class* annals.sources.FolderSource(root, \*, name, title=None, exclude=('.\*', '_\_pycache_\_', '\*.pyc', '\*.pyo'), session_of=<function top_level_name>)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

A folder of files, read in place and never written, as a `Mapping` of rows.

Keys are paths relative to `root` (`"annals.md"`, `"cw-liaise/design.md"`), values
listing rows. The folder is walked on every listing (a stat per file, cheap for
hundreds), and a file is re-read only when its size or mtime changed. Hidden files and
caches are skipped (`exclude`, the same patterns a directory publish skips), and so
is anything that resolves outside `root`.

`session_of(rel)` names who wrote a file; the default suits a folder of per-session
files and sub-folders ([`top_level_name()`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#annals.sources.top_level_name)).

#### file_path(rel)

The file on disk; `KeyError` if it is absent, hidden, or escapes the root.

Only the canonical spelling of a path is accepted (`a/b.md`, not `./a/b.md`,
`a//b.md` or `a/b.md/`), so one file has one key.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

#### text(rel)

The file’s text (cached until it changes); `""` for binaries and huge files.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The documents agents published, as rows (a view over a `DocStore`).

# _autosummary/annals.store.html.md

# annals.store

The document store: a flat set of documents, tags, groups and a recycle bin, as plain files.

Layout under the data root (local or remote, see [`annals.target`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#module-annals.target)):

```default
docs/<id>/meta.json         one document: metadata
docs/<id>/<main file>       its content (index.html, report.md, ...), plus any assets
docs/<id>/.versions/<n>/    an earlier version, whole (its own meta.json and files)
docs/<id>.r<stamp>-<hex>/   a replacement not applied yet (``publish(replace=<id>)``)
trash/<id>/...              the same shape; the recycle bin is a move
groups/<gid>.json           a named, ordered list of document ids with its own URL
```

Flat on purpose: agents from many corpora do not share a hierarchy, and every placement
decision costs tokens. Tags and groups carry the structure. Ids are time-sortable and
readable (`20261003-203301-starwars-theme-report-3f9a`), so a listing is already in
publication order and a URL says what it points to.

Plain files, written whole, because the same tree is written by rsync from another machine
and read by the server; there is no index to keep consistent.

Living documents (one link that stays current) are a replace: the new files are written as
a *pending* replacement next to the document, never over it, and whoever reads the store
applies it ([`DocStore.settle()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore.settle)): the current files move under `.versions/<n>/` and
the replacement takes the id. Writing beside rather than over is what lets a replace travel
through an outbox (a directory another machine pulls and empties): the pending directory is
just another new directory to pull, and the store on the reading side applies it. Applying
is a sequence of renames, each claimed atomically, so two readers never apply the same
replacement twice and nothing is ever deleted.

### Module Attributes

| [`HEAD_CHARS`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.HEAD_CHARS)      | how much of a file is read to find its title and excerpt                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_EXCLUDE`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DFLT_EXCLUDE)    | hidden files, caches, compiled python                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`VERSIONS`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.VERSIONS)        | a published folder's own content skips hidden names, and a document that carries one anyway is refused)                                                                                                                                           |
| [`VERSION_SEP`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.VERSION_SEP)     | `<id>@<n>` names version `n` of a document; `@` is not an id character                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`PENDING_SEP`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.PENDING_SEP)     | `<id>.r<stamp>-<hex>` is a pending replacement of `<id>`                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`LOCK_PREFIX`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.LOCK_PREFIX)     | `<root>/.lock-<id>/` is held while a replacement of `<id>` is applied; it is also the working directory, holding `next` (the replacement) and `old` (the version being archived) between renames, and `lock.json` (what a recovery needs to know) |
| [`LOCK_STALE_S`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.LOCK_STALE_S)    | its work is finished or undone                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

#### meta(doc_id, , settle=True)

One document’s meta; `in_trash` says which side of the bin it is on.

`<id>@<n>` is version `n`: its own meta, with `version_of` naming the document.
A pending replacement, read by its own id, says `pending`. `settle=False`
skips applying pending replacements (for a hot path such as a raw file).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### pending(doc_id=None, , names=None)

`names`: the listing of `docs/` when the caller already has it.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore.list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### publish(\*sources, title=None, tags=(), source=None, text=None, filename='document.md', exclude=('.\*', '_\_pycache_\_', '\*.pyc', '\*.pyo'), replace=None, artifact=None)

Publish files (or a directory, or `text`) as ONE document; return its meta.

One markdown or html file is the common case. A directory is published whole, with
`index.html` (or the first renderable file) as the page shown. `text` publishes a
string as `filename` instead of reading sources. `exclude` lists glob patterns
skipped inside a directory (hidden files and caches by default; `()` keeps all).

`replace` (a document id) publishes a new version of that document instead of a
new document: same id, same link, the current files kept as a version. It is
written as a pending replacement and applied at once when this store settles
(otherwise where the store is read). The returned meta says `pending` until then.

`artifact` (a claude.ai artifact link, see [`check_artifact_url()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.check_artifact_url)) is the
interactive version of the page: the document’s page links out to it. A
replacement that names none keeps the document’s current one.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

Delete a document that is in the bin. Refuses one that is not.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

* **Return type:**

Case-insensitive match of every query word against title, tags, excerpt, source.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore.list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### settle(doc_id=None)

A replacement whose document is not here yet (it is still on its way, or the

# _autosummary/annals.tags.html.md

# annals.tags

The owner’s tags: a `MutableMapping` from item key to tag list, kept apart from the items.

Tags the owner adds on the page are stored here, never in the items themselves: a folder
source belongs to whoever writes it (a crowsnest ledger belongs to its session), so annals
must not edit it, and a published document’s `meta.json` is the publisher’s record.
An entry, once present, is the item’s whole tag list (it replaces the item’s own tags, so
removing a tag the publisher set works too); deleting the entry falls back to them.

[`JsonTagStore`](_autosummary/annals.tags.html.md#annals.tags.JsonTagStore), the default, is one JSON file under the data root
(`<data root>/tags/tags.json`), written atomically. Any `MutableMapping[str, list[str]]`
can replace it (`mk_api(tags=...)`), e.g. a table in a database.

### Functions

| [`normalize_tags`](_autosummary/annals.tags.html.md#annals.tags.normalize_tags)(tags)   | Trimmed, single-spaced, de-duplicated (ignoring case), sorted; refuses junk.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`JsonTagStore`](_autosummary/annals.tags.html.md#annals.tags.JsonTagStore)(path)   | `{item key: [tags]}` in one JSON file, re-read when another process changed it.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* annals.tags.JsonTagStore(path)

Bases: [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

`{item key: [tags]}` in one JSON file, re-read when another process changed it.

Safe with several server processes on one machine: a write takes an exclusive
`flock` on `<file>.lock`, re-reads the file, changes it and replaces it atomically,
so two workers saving at once never lose each other’s change. A read re-reads the file
whenever its inode, size or mtime changed (every write makes a new inode).

#### snapshot()

Every entry at once, under one read (what a listing overlays).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### annals.tags.normalize_tags(tags)

Trimmed, single-spaced, de-duplicated (ignoring case), sorted; refuses junk.

Raises `ValueError` for a tag that is not a string, is longer than `MAX_TAG_LEN`,
holds control characters, or for more than `MAX_TAGS_PER_ITEM` tags.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/annals.target.html.md

# annals.target

The transport seam: a document tree lands in a directory, here or on another machine.

A `Target` is the handful of filesystem verbs the store needs (put a directory, move,
remove, read and write a text file, list sub-directories, read every `meta.json` under a
directory). Two implementations:

* [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.LocalTarget): a directory on this machine, plain `pathlib`/`shutil`.
* [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.SshTarget): `host:path` on another machine, through the system `ssh` and
  `rsync` in batch mode (no prompts, so an agent never hangs). The host is whatever the
  user’s `~/.ssh/config` resolves, so an alias such as `tw` works.

[`parse_target()`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.parse_target) picks one from a string. An HTTP target (a bearer-token ingest
endpoint) is the declared replacement for the ssh one and is not built yet.

### Module Attributes

| [`RECORD_SEP`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.RECORD_SEP)   | Separator between concatenated meta.json files when reading many at once over ssh.                                  |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`LOCK_NOTE`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.LOCK_NOTE)    | the note a lock directory is created with (see [`Target.make_lock()`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.Target.make_lock)) |

### Functions

| [`check_rel`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.check_rel)(rel)     | Refuse anything that could escape the root; the store only ever passes safe paths.                                                                                |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`parse_target`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.parse_target)(spec) | `host:/path` becomes an [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.SshTarget); anything else a [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.LocalTarget). |

### Classes

| [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.LocalTarget)(root)          | A directory on this machine.                                                |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.SshTarget)(host, root)      | `host:path` on another machine, via the system ssh and rsync in batch mode. |
| [`Target`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.Target)(\*args, \*\*kwargs) | What the store needs from wherever the documents live.                      |

the note a lock directory is created with (see [`Target.make_lock()`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.Target.make_lock))

Separator between concatenated meta.json files when reading many at once over ssh.

# _autosummary/annals.tools.html.md

# annals.tools

The operations, as plain functions: JSON-able arguments in, JSON-able dicts out.

This module is the single source of truth for what a annals can do. The CLI
(`annals.__main__`, via `cw`), the MCP server (`py2mcp` over string refs to these
names) and the shipped skill all describe the same functions, so there is nothing to keep
in parity. Nothing here prints or exits; the surfaces do that.

### Functions

| [`configure`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.configure)(\*[, target, base_url, to, outbox, ...])   | Write the publisher config (where to publish, what link to print) and show it.         |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`copy`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.copy)(refs, \*, to[, source, target, base_url])       | Copy documents or groups to a named target, keeping their ids; print the new link.     |
| [`group`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.group)(title, doc_ids, \*[, target, base_url, to])    | Make a group (one URL for a set of documents) from existing document ids.              |
| [`groups`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.groups)(\*[, target, base_url, to])                   | List groups, newest first.                                                             |
| [`ls`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.ls)([q, trash, limit, target, base_url, to])          | List documents (newest first), optionally filtered by words or showing the bin.        |
| [`page_shell`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.page_shell)(\*[, api, base, title])                   | The page's html shell, for a host that serves the API under its own prefix.            |
| [`publish`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.publish)(paths, \*[, title, tags, group, ...])        | Publish one document and print its link; several paths become several documents.       |
| [`restore`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.restore)(doc_ids, \*[, target, to])                   | Bring documents back from the recycle bin.                                             |
| [`serve`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.serve)(\*[, host, port, data_dir, base_path, ...])    | Serve the annals page and API (needs `pip install 'annals[server]'`).                  |
| [`share`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.share)(ref, \*[, password, expires, include, ...])    | Make a public link to ONE document (or group) and print it; nothing else is reachable. |
| [`shares`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.shares)(\*[, all, target, base_url, to])              | List share links, newest first (`all`: revoked and expired ones too).                  |
| [`show`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.show)(doc_id, \*[, target, base_url, to])             | A document's metadata and link (`to`: on a named target).                              |
| [`trash`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.trash)(doc_ids, \*[, target, to])                     | Move documents to the recycle bin (restorable).                                        |
| [`unshare`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.unshare)(links, \*[, target, to])                     | Revoke share links (their token or full link): they stop working at once.              |

### annals.tools.configure(, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, outbox=False, share_base_url=None)

Write the publisher config (where to publish, what link to print) and show it.

### Example

`annals configure --target tw:/root/.local/share/annals --base-url https://apps.example.com/annals`.
`--to NAME` saves the target and base url as a named target (`annals publish --to NAME`)
and leaves the default alone. `--outbox` marks the target as an outbox: a directory
the server pulls and empties (it cannot be written to from here), so replacements are
left for the server to apply; it is kept by later changes (`ANNALS_OUTBOX=0` or an
edit of the file turns it off). `--share-base-url` is where share links point when
the share server is not at `<base-url>/shared` (a platform running it as its own
public app). With no arguments, shows the resolved settings without writing.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.copy(refs, , to, source=None, target=None, base_url=None)

Copy documents or groups to a named target, keeping their ids; print the new link.

`refs` are links (`https://.../annals/d/<id>`, `.../g/<group-id>`) or bare ids; only
the id is used, so the link may point at any instance. They are read from the default
target (or the named target `source`) and written to the named target `to`. A group
is copied with its documents and keeps its id and title. Copying again refreshes the
copy. The source must be readable from this machine (a directory, or `host:/path`).
`target`/`base_url` override the DESTINATION’s location, as in `publish`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.group(title, doc_ids, , target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

Make a group (one URL for a set of documents) from existing document ids.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.groups(, target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

List groups, newest first.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.ls(q='', , trash=False, limit=50, target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

List documents (newest first), optionally filtered by words or showing the bin.

`to` lists a named target instead of the default one.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.page_shell(, api='/api/annals', base='/annals', title='annals')

The page’s html shell, for a host that serves the API under its own prefix.

An enlace app writes it once as its frontend:
`annals page-shell --api /api/annals --base /annals > frontend/index.html`.
The shell only names the two paths; the page’s code loads from the API, so it upgrades
with the package.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.tools.publish(paths, , title=None, tags='', group=None, add_to=None, session=None, all_files=False, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, replace=None, artifact=None)

Publish one document and print its link; several paths become several documents.

`paths`: files of any kind (markdown, html, images, video, audio, pdf, text), a
directory (one document: an `index.html` or single page with its assets, else a
gallery of everything in it), or `-` for stdin (markdown). `tags` is comma separated. `group`
names a group to create from the published documents; the reply then carries
`group_url` too. `add_to` appends them to an existing group instead (its id, as
printed in a group link), so a second batch lands under the link the owner already has. `session` records who published (the source shown on the page). A directory skips
hidden files and caches (`.*`, `__pycache__`, `*.pyc`) unless `all_files`.
`to` publishes to a named target of the config file (`[targets.NAME]`, see
`annals configure --to`) instead of the default one. `replace` (a document’s link or
id) publishes ONE path as a new version of that document: the link stays the same, the
page shows the new version and offers the earlier ones. That is how a living page (a
guide, a status page) keeps one link. `artifact` (a claude.ai artifact link) is the
interactive version of the page: the document’s page shows an “Open the interactive
version” button. Publish the Artifact first, then the same page here with its link.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.restore(doc_ids, , target=None, to=None)

Bring documents back from the recycle bin.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.serve(, host='127.0.0.1', port=8765, data_dir=None, base_path='/annals', allow_open=False)

Serve the annals page and API (needs `pip install 'annals[server]'`).

Auth comes from the environment: `ANNALS_WHOAMI_URL` + `ANNALS_ALLOWED_USERS` to sit
behind an existing login, `ANNALS_BASIC_USER` + `ANNALS_BASIC_PASSWORD` for HTTP Basic,
nothing for an open server on localhost. A host reachable beyond this machine with no auth
configured is refused unless `allow_open` (`--allow-open`) says something else gates it.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### annals.tools.share(ref, , password=None, expires='7d', include=None, exclude=None, title=None, target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

Make a public link to ONE document (or group) and print it; nothing else is reachable.

`ref` is a document or group id, or its link. The link opens without a login, shows
only that page and the files chosen, and can be revoked (`annals unshare`).
`include`: comma separated files of the document to share (the page itself always
is), or ids of other annals pages it links to; by default every file of the document
(for a group: every document; `include` then picks documents). `exclude` drops
files. `expires` (7 days unless told): `12h`, `30d`, `2w`, a date (`2026-11-01`,
through that day, UTC), an ISO time, or `never`. `password` gates the link (stored hashed; `-` reads it from
stdin, so it stays out of the shell history).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.shares(, all=False, target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

List share links, newest first (`all`: revoked and expired ones too).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.show(doc_id, , target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

A document’s metadata and link (`to`: on a named target).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.trash(doc_ids, , target=None, to=None)

Move documents to the recycle bin (restorable).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.unshare(links, , target=None, to=None)

Revoke share links (their token or full link): they stop working at once.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# For AI agents

`annals` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `annals-publish`

Publish a document or media (a markdown report, an html page, images, video, audio, a PDF, or a whole folder of renders) to the owner’s private annals and hand back the link, so they can read it on a phone or tablet away from the terminal. Use whenever the user asks to “publish this”, “post it to my annals”, “put it where I can read it on my phone”, “give me a link to that report”, “show me the images”, “where can I see the renders”, “share the page with me”, or whenever you have produced a document longer than a few lines that the user will want to read later or elsewhere. Also covers living pages (one link that stays current: `--replace`), grouping several documents under one link, listing what is in the annals, and moving a document to the recycle bin.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/annals annals-publish --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`annals/data/skills/annals-publish`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/annals/tree/HEAD/annals/data/skills/annals-publish) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install annals`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/annals/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`annals.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/annals/annals.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/annals/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
